events.title: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
events.description: British forces under General James Wolfe defeated French forces under the Marquis de Montcalm on a field outside Quebec City. The battle lasted about 15 minutes, and both commanders were mortally wounded.
events.significance: The British victory led to the fall of Quebec and effectively decided the French and Indian War in North America, paving the way for British control of Canada.

events.title: Bombardment of Fort McHenry Begins
events.description: British naval forces began a 25-hour bombardment of Fort McHenry in Baltimore Harbor during the War of 1812. Francis Scott Key, watching from a ship, saw the American flag still flying at dawn on September 14.
events.significance: The event inspired Key to write the poem 'Defence of Fort McHenry', which became the lyrics of 'The Star-Spangled Banner', the U.S. national anthem since 1931.

events.title: U.S. Confederation Congress Sets Date for First Federal Elections
events.description: The Confederation Congress passed a resolution setting the dates for choosing presidential electors and for the first meeting of government under the new Constitution, with New York City as the seat of government.
events.significance: This step moved the United States from the Articles of Confederation to government under the Constitution, with George Washington's election as first president soon following.

events.title: Margaret Chase Smith Elected to U.S. Senate
events.description: Margaret Chase Smith won election to the U.S. Senate from Maine, becoming the first woman to serve in both houses of Congress. She was a Republican and later gave her 'Declaration of Conscience' speech in 1950.
events.significance: Her election was a milestone for women in American politics, and her 1950 speech was an early rebuke of McCarthyism.

events.title: Attica Prison Uprising Ends
events.description: New York State Police and corrections officers retook Attica Correctional Facility after inmates had held it for four days, demanding better conditions and political rights. The assault left 43 people dead, including 10 hostages.
events.significance: The uprising became a landmark in the debate over prison conditions and the treatment of inmates in the U.S., prompting calls for reform.
